summary: The three prose fixes hold and I am content for this to govern my output -- the Never-cut bullet now names provenance and explicitly carves 'I did not run this; by inspection' out of the Hedging clause, which was the exact pressure my r1 T1 named; the out-of-scope carve-out resolves T2 by explicit exception even though the section preamble's 'persist beyond the conversation' predicate still matches a verdict in .harness/review/; and test-reviewer.md's review.sh claim is accurate, verified at scripts/review.sh:263-264, and does not overclaim (it says REFUSES a finding with NO failure_scenario, and non-emptiness is exactly what the script checks). T3 (tokenizer) stays acceptable unfixed: the three rules are correct on readability alone, so a reader who disbelieves the arithmetic still follows them; it does not need a caveat and is not worth a round, though the file now demands provenance for a measured claim on line 43 while asserting three unmeasured ones on lines 49-54. What blocks is not the prose. Between r1 and this hash a 208-line ADR for a DIFFERENT backlog row was staged into this commit, and that row is still todo in the same diff. Round two's own rule applies literally: the commit is too big, so it is split rather than reviewed again. The ADR itself is not defective -- I verified six of its test-facing claims against the tree and all six hold -- it is misfiled.

findings.title: M4.10b's deliverable is staged into M0.79's commit, while M4.10b stays `todo` in the same diff
findings.failure_scenario: M0.79 is 'LAND THE `brevity` SKILL AND ITS ADAPTER'. `git diff --stat 73bbbb561fe7b5 $(git write-tree)` -- r1's recorded staged_tree against this index -- shows this 208-line file added since the round that carries a verdict. backlog.md:124 still reads 'M4.10b | DECIDE THE IDEMPOTENCY KEY AND WHICH FORMATS CHANGE, as an ADR ... | FR-3 | todo', and the only backlog edit in this diff adds the M0.79 row; M4.10b's status is untouched. Concrete downstream failure: after this lands, the tree carries `Status: accepted` ADR-0036 for a decision no task records as done. A later session runs `next-task`, is handed M4.10b, and either re-derives a decision that already exists or files ADR-0037 against it -- the duplication ADRs exist to prevent. Nothing catches it: `check-commit-msg.sh` only requires the subject name a real ID, and M0.79 is real; `check-reviewed.sh` binds the hash, so a verdict recorded here launders the ADR as reviewed under a task whose row does not mention it. Surviving mutation of the staged bytes, which is the proof it is not part of M0.79: `git restore --staged docs/internal/product/decisions/0036-*.md` and every gate the packet lists as PASSED still passes -- check-links, check-file-size, check-archive-row-size, check-session-load, build-index.sh --check, check-terminology, check-license-headers -- because none of them reads this file, and no file in the M0.79 change set references 0036 (grep for '0036' across docs/, .agents/ and AGENTS.md returns only the file itself). Resolution is mechanical and is the split round two prescribes: unstage the ADR, land M0.79, land the ADR under M4.10b with its row flipped. NOT a defect in the ADR: I checked its six test-facing claims and all hold -- sequencer/src/test/java/binjava/sequencer/BatchingSequencerTest.java:261 asserts only `hasSize(2)` on a two-pod `commitAll`; format/src/test/java/binjava/format/BatchedCommitDeltaTest.java:43-45 round-trips three segments under three pod prefixes; format/src/test/resources/golden/chain-delta-batched-v1.bin holds `bins/a.seg` and `bins/b.seg` with no pod in either; format/src/test/java/binjava/format/CheckpointTest.java:169 asserts `isLessThan(64 * 1024)` at 1,600 streams; format/src/main/java/binjava/format/Checkpoint.java:151 is `if (version != VERSION)`, a strict equality check as stated; CheckpointDecodeRefusalTest.java:117 is `bytes[7] = 1`.

findings.title: The `.agents/` mirror closes the output-style gap for the test reviewer only, and names a third, different protected set
findings.failure_scenario: The stated reason for this hunk is that a tool reading only `.agents/` would run a reviewer with no output-style rule. Line 103 is the file's ONLY occurrence of `brevity` -- it sits under '## What the test reviewer looks for' (line 99). The production reviewer's section, '## What to look for' (line 63), still has none. So that tool now runs `test-reviewer` with an output-style rule and `reviewer` with none: the gap is closed for one of the two roles and the commit reads as though it were closed for both. Second, three protected sets now exist where the brief says the format is not overridden: .claude/agents/reviewer.md:37 names {file:line, severity, concrete failure scenario}; .claude/agents/test-reviewer.md:62 names {file:line, severity, concrete failure scenario, surviving mutation}; .agents/skills/review/SKILL.md:103 names those four PLUS 'whether a result was measured or inferred'. The brief a Claude Code subagent actually loads is test-reviewer.md -- I am running from it -- so the provenance clause my r1 T1 asked for reaches me through brevity/SKILL.md's Never-cut list and through this mirror, but NOT through the enumerated 'stay, in full' list that an agent under compression pressure consults when deciding what to shorten. That is the same asymmetry T4 named for `failure_scenario` and it was fixed there by adding the item to the list. Surviving mutation: delete lines 103-107 in full and `build-index.sh --check`, `check-links.sh`, `check-portability.sh`, `check-rule-citations.sh` and `check-session-load.sh` all still pass -- no gate reads this section's body, build-index compares index rows to frontmatter descriptions, and check-rule-citations resolves rule NAMES, none of which this hunk adds or removes. Nothing in the tree can distinguish the mirror's presence from its absence, which is why the fork can widen silently.
